label: Linux OS telemetry

corePack.why: CPU saturation is the first host-level capacity signal.
corePack.whyNow: Sustained high CPU becomes user-visible latency.
corePack.metric: Average CPU used percent by host

corePack.why: Memory pressure precedes OOM killer and swapping storms.
corePack.whyNow: Catch hosts before the kernel starts killing processes.

corePack.why: Disk fill is a preventable availability failure on every Linux host.
corePack.whyNow: Full disks stop logging, databases, and packages at once.

corePack.why: SSH brute force is the default identity attack on Linux servers.
corePack.whyNow: Auth failures are both security and availability (lockouts).

corePack.why: Systemd unit failures are service crashes on modern Linux.
corePack.whyNow: A crashed unit is an application outage with a host-local cause.

corePack.why: OOM killer events are the kernel's last resort after memory pressure.
corePack.whyNow: Process kills without this signal look like random crashes.

valueHypothesis: Linux as a product means OS telemetry: CPU, memory, disk, authentication failures, and service crashes. HCI, ISE, or NGFW use cases that mention Linux in passing are out of this pack.
rationale: Unix/Linux monitoring practice and Splunk_TA_nix scripted inputs exist for CPU, memory, disk, secure logs, and service health. Ranking must not treat every Linux string in the catalogue as a core OS use case.
